title: Journey to the West 西遊記
story: The monkey hero’s surname is the word for macaque with its animal part taken off. The novel hides more monkeys in his stable title and calls him the mind-monkey. Arthur Waley’s 1942 English called him Monkey, and in 2021 that is still his English name.

lines.said: In the Chinese novel Journey to the West, the monkey hero’s surname comes from the word for macaque, with the animal part removed.
lines.screen: A box closes round 西遊記 on the chapter 1 title column. Cut to the naming passage, where 猢猻 is boxed and lifted to the middle of the frame.

lines.said: Without the animal part, the second character leaves boy and infant, so his surname is Sun.
lines.screen: The animal radical lifts off. 孫 opens into 子 (boy) and 系 (infant), closes again, and “Sun” is typed under it.

lines.said: In 1942 Arthur Waley’s English translation left this out, and a footnote translated Sun as Monkey.
lines.screen: The tag ARTHUR WALEY, 1942 rises. A hairline runs from “Sun” to the word “Monkey,” labelled footnote.

lines.said: Waley called the book Monkey too.
lines.screen: Back to the title column. The title “Monkey” is typed in the film’s own type, with a hairline to 西遊記.

lines.said: He kept thirty of the hundred chapters.
lines.screen: The 1592 contents. Seventy columns fall to tint while the counter runs from 100 of 100 to 30 of 100.

lines.said: In the novel, Heaven gives the monkey a post in the imperial stables.
lines.screen: The chapter 4 woodcut of the court audience, with a slow push in.
The title is boxed in the chapter 4 text. It travels up, a copy drops below, and the copy’s characters swap to 避馬瘟.
Both rows stand with the shared reading between them, so one sound is heard under two spellings.

lines.said: The title is usually heard as ward off horse plague.
lines.screen: “ward off horse plague” is typed under 避馬瘟.

lines.said: Chinese stables kept a macaque for that job.
lines.screen: The horse manual’s line quoted in the Compendium of Materia Medica is set in Chinese type. 母猴 is boxed as “macaque,” and a hairline joins it to the title.

lines.said: In the oldest surviving edition, the chapter titles call him the mind-monkey.
lines.screen: The chapter 14 contents. 心猿 is boxed and lifted, and “mind-monkey” is typed under it.

lines.said: The scholar Hu Shih introduced Waley’s book to Americans as humour and satire, freed from allegorical readings.
lines.screen: Hu Shih’s 1939 photograph stands at the right while 心猿 stays untouched at the left, so the two readings sit side by side.

lines.said: Waley’s Monkey travels west with Pigsy the pig, Sandy the river monster and Tripitaka the monk.
lines.screen: Timothy Richard’s 1913 plates arrive one at a time, each on its spoken name, with Waley’s name typed under it.

lines.said: In 2021 Julia Lovell’s translation kept all four names, and its hero is still Monkey.
lines.screen: Lovell’s row of names is set under Waley’s. A box closes round both rows, then a second box closes round the two “Monkey” entries.
